propositions: When multiple bundles exist for a single S3 ref, git ls-remote returns the ref at multiple SHAs and fresh clones fail with 'multiple updates for ref not allowed', rendering the store unclonable.

git-remote-s3's cmd_push rejects all ref operations while bundles > 1 before writing anything, causing rebar's push path to stall; retries cannot converge because fetch cannot resolve the ambiguous ref.

Upstream's interactive Doctor.fix_multiple_bundles blocks on input() and discards the non-chosen head via side-branching or deletion, causing events unique to that head to be permanently lost from the append-only store.

Rebar's sync._do_reconverge/_union_merge already implements lossless 2-parent merges for divergent git-remote heads by treating them as per-target ref divergence; the S3 multi-bundle case is the same divergence hidden at the bundle-storage layer.

The heal must write the merged tip as a NEW bundle before deleting any original bundles and never delete the merged tip itself, so at every crash point at least one bundle carries the full merged history; mid-delete crashes re-heal to a single lossless bundle on the next run.

Concurrent heal attempts must serialize via the helper's per-ref lock (acquire_lock/release_lock with IfNoneMatch conditional-put); a process that cannot acquire the lock backs off without healing and converges on the winner's collapsed single bundle within the same push retry loop.
